# Operator decisions

Decisions the operator (@robotat-com) made that change how the build runs. Where this file and a `PHASE-*.md` spec disagree, this file wins. Every build agent reads it together with `project.yaml`.

| # | Date | Decision | Overrides |
|---|---|---|---|
| OD-1 | 2026-10-21 | **No date targets.** The build runs milestone by milestone, phase by phase, as fast as the gates allow. Dates in specs and in `project.yaml` `schedule` are informational. | Calendars in `PHASE-*.md` 1.8 |
| OD-2 | 2026-10-21 | **The orchestrating session merges agent pull requests.** A Claude Code session started by the operator orchestrates the build: it starts one builder per milestone, runs an independent review, and merges the pull request once (1) every acceptance command passed and the evidence is in the pull request, (2) every review finding that affects correctness, requirements or guardrails is fixed, and (3) CI is green (from M1.6 on). It merges with `gh pr merge <n> --merge` only: no squash, no rebase, no `--admin`, no `--delete-branch`, no `--auto`. The operator reviews merged work afterwards. | PHASE-1.md 0.2, 1.9, 2.2 step 11, 2.5 item 8, 2.6 (merging only) |
| OD-3 | 2026-10-21 | **Milestone builders still never merge**, never push to `main`, never force-push, never delete remote branches and never change repository settings. A builder stops when its pull request is open, as 2.2 says. | Nothing |
| OD-4 | 2026-10-21 | **Independent review runs as a separate agent** started by the orchestrator after the builder opens its pull request, because a builder cannot start its own subagents. It uses the instructions in `.claude/agents/reviewer.md` (and `contract-guardian.md` or `aml-claims-checker.md` where 2.2 step 7 says so) once M1.2 has created them. Fixes go onto the same branch before the merge. | PHASE-1.md 2.2 step 7 (order only) |
| OD-5 | 2026-10-21 | **Human sign-offs stay human.** The orchestrator never freezes a contract or creates the `contracts-v*` tag, never sets a typology to `approved`, never sets an ADR to `accepted`, never confirms a licence decision, and never writes learning logs, self-assessments, teach-backs, exit posts or assignment submissions. It pauses at each point that needs one of these and asks the operator, in one batch per gate. | Nothing |
| OD-6 | 2026-10-21 | **One person holds every role for now.** @robotat-com is project lead, tech lead, mentor of every squad, data steward, typology researcher, technical writer, demo producer, community manager and release manager until the team joins. `people.interns` is empty, so gate checks that count interns (GC-11, GC-12, GC-13 in Phase 1) are reported as not met, and the operator decides at the gate. | `project.yaml` `people` |
| OD-7 | 2026-10-21 | **Organisation move pending.** The repository is `robotat-com/neon-radar` until the operator creates the `neonradar` organisation and it is transferred; `project.yaml` already names `neonradar/neon-radar` and the `@neonradar/nr-*` teams. `gh` follows the git remote, so commands work before and after the move. | PHASE-1.md 1.1 (repository name `neon-radar`, not `neonradar`) |
| OD-8 | 2026-10-21 | **Wording about how the project is built must be true.** Wherever a file says humans merge every change (for example the README "How we build" paragraph, `CONTRIBUTING.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), it says instead that during the initial build the operator authorised the orchestrating agent session to merge after acceptance checks, independent review and CI, that humans review merged work, and that humans own every decision in OD-5. | PHASE-1.md M1.1 and M1.2 wording |
| OD-9 | 2026-10-21 | **Merge guard follows OD-2.** In M1.2, `guard_git.py`, the `.claude/settings.json` deny rules and `scripts/test_hooks.sh` allow exactly `gh pr merge <number> --merge` (optionally with `--repo <owner>/<name>`, `--subject` or `--body`) and keep blocking every other `gh pr merge` form, every `gh api` call that merges or moves refs, pushes to `main`, force-pushes, remote branch deletion and settings changes. | PHASE-1.md M1.2 (guard rules and their tests) |
| OD-10 | 2026-10-21 | **Autopilot.** The operator told the orchestrator to proceed on its recommended options without asking. Decisions OD-11 to OD-15 were taken that way and are listed for the operator's review at Gate 1. The OD-5 sign-offs still wait for a human. | Nothing |
| OD-11 | 2026-10-21 | **Record ids use FollowTheMoney's reference alphabet.** C1 rule R1 is `<prefix>-<rest>` with `rest` matching `[A-Za-z0-9.-]{0,99}[A-Za-z0-9]` (M1.7a, PR #8), so every valid id can be referenced. Loaders map source ids that contain `_`, `:` or other characters into this alphabet and keep the native id in `nr.source_ref`. The tech lead signs this off at Gate 1. | PHASE-1.md 4.4 and 5.1 (id pattern) |
| OD-12 | 2026-10-21 | **Never use "Cedar Gate Holdings Ltd".** The synthetic company in the PHASE-1.md 5.4 alert example matches a live UK company (Companies House search, 21 Oct 2026). Every milestone that would use it picks another name. Before any synthetic company or person name is committed, check it against the public Companies House search (`find-and-update.company-information.service.gov.uk/search/companies?q=`), and record the query, the date and the result in the pull request. Guardrail G1. | PHASE-1.md 5.4 example and any fixture that copies it |
| OD-13 | 2026-10-21 | **GDS is a pinned jar, not part of the image.** The Neo4j 5.26 Community image bundles APOC Core but not GDS. `make plugins` downloads GDS 2.13.4 once (SHA-256 pinned) into `data/cache/neo4j-plugins/`, and `make up` never downloads anything (G3). Testcontainers and CI should mount the same jar rather than set `NEO4J_PLUGINS` to include GDS. | PHASE-1.md 3.1, M1.4 step 2, any test that expects a bundled GDS |
| OD-14 | 2026-10-21 | **Agents never create, read or edit `.env`.** The operator runs `bash scripts/ensure_env.sh` in the main checkout (after deleting the empty `.env` left by M1.4's first run) and adds `CH_API_KEY` there. Until then, a milestone that needs a database uses Testcontainers or a throwaway password passed through the environment, never written to a file. | PHASE-1.md M1.4 and later milestones that say "create `.env`" |
| OD-15 | 2026-10-21 | **The orchestrator may grant `size-exception`** to a milestone on the critical path, instead of splitting it into serial pull requests, when the review still covers the whole diff. Each such pull request says so. | PHASE-1.md 2.3 (split rule) |
| OD-16 | 2026-10-21 | **The protection script does not block merges.** On this plan, `scripts/setup_repo_protection.sh` can change little (GitHub returns 403 for branch protection on private Free repositories). The operator runs it when convenient, again after the organisation move (OD-7), and at launch. Until then, CI is not enforced by GitHub; the orchestrating session checks `gh pr checks` before every merge (OD-2). | PHASE-1.md M1.6 (protection before merge) |
| OD-17 | 2026-10-21 | **`contracts/C1-record.md` is the authority for the record format.** Where it differs from PHASE-1.md 4.4, 5.1 or the M1.8 instructions, the merged contract document wins. That covers the id alphabet and `make_id`, Payment dates written as UTC with no `Z`, ISO 4217 currencies, `nr.address_roles` on the LegalEntity, Companies House officer and PSC ids, duplicate ids, reference ranges, and which topics synthetic records may carry. The same applies to each later contract document (`C2-graph-schema.md`, C3, C4) once it is merged. | PHASE-1.md 4.4, 5.1, M1.8a–e wording |
